accepted.question_text: Let f: I -> R be a convex C^infinity function on an interval I, and for a < b in I define N(alpha, beta) = alpha(f(a) + f(b)) + beta f((a + b)/2) with 2alpha + beta = 1. Determine the best possible constants alpha* and beta* for which the upper Hermite-Hadamard-type inequality (1/(b - a)) integral_a^b f(t) dt <= N(alpha*, beta*) holds for every such smooth convex function and every choice of a < b in I. Equivalently, find the smallest universal endpoint weight alpha* such that alpha*(f(a) + f(b)) + (1 - 2alpha*) f((a + b)/2) always dominates the integral mean of every smooth convex function. The paper shows that N(1/4, 1/2) works for all convex integrable functions, and that the sharper candidate N(1/6, 2/3) is best possible only under the additional assumption that f'' is convex (equivalently, f^(4) >= 0), so the universal optimum for all smooth convex functions remains open.
accepted.context_brief: Best universal upper bound refining Hermite-Hadamard

evidence.quote: We found the value N(1/4, 1/2) for which the right-hand side of (1.3) holds for any integrable convex function.

Therefore we obtain a potentially best possible bound N(1/6, 2/3). Unfortunately, as is shown in Theorem 2.6, this bound is best possible only for the class of differentiable convex functions for which f^(4)(t) >= 0, t in I.
Open Question Find the best possible bound N(alpha*, beta*) valid for all convex mappings from the class C^infinity(I).
